info.title: What changes
info.aggregated: The reference currency decides which currency is used to add up totals that mix accounts/assets in different currencies — net worth, portfolio value, overall income/expenses.

intro.title: Before you connect: you need a Google Cloud project
intro.description: Lumio is self-hosted: unlike a service with a single domain, it can't ship with ready-made Google credentials (Google requires a return address registered in advance, different for every installation). Whoever runs this instance creates their own project — free, one-time, about 10 minutes — exactly as already done for an optional AI or market data provider.

steps.createProject: Create the project. At the top next to the "Google Cloud" logo, open the project selector → New project. Any name works (e.g. "my-lumio") → Create, then select it as the active project.
steps.enableApis: Enable the APIs. Menu ☰ → APIs & services → Library. Search for and enable Google Sheets API, Google Drive API, and Google Picker API (all three: the Picker API must be enabled separately, Drive alone isn't enough — otherwise it won't show up in the list when you restrict the key in step 5).
steps.consentScreen: Configure the OAuth consent screen. Menu ☰ → APIs & services → OAuth consent screen. User type External. In the "Test users" section add your Gmail address: this keeps you in "Testing" mode, without needing Google's review — perfect for personal use.
steps.createCredentialsIntro: Create the OAuth credentials. APIs & services → Credentials → Create credentials → OAuth client ID, type Web application. In the authorized redirect URI paste exactly:
steps.createCredentialsOutro: Create, then copy the client ID and client secret.
steps.pickerKey: Create the Picker key (Drive folder selection). Still in Credentials → Create credentials → API key, then restrict it (Edit → API restrictions) to Google Picker API only.
steps.pasteValues: Paste the 4 values (client ID, client secret, the URI above, the Picker key) into this instance's .env file — variables GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID, GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET, GOOGLE_REDIRECT_URI, GOOGLE_PICKER_API_KEY (and VITE_GOOGLE_PICKER_API_KEY for the frontend) — then restart the Docker containers.

info.title: Two categories of job
info.scheduled: Scheduled jobs run on their own at fixed intervals (a cron), no matter what you do in the app — which is why they have a real on/off switch here. Turning one off only stops the automatic run: wherever an equivalent manual button exists (e.g. "Refresh now"), that one always stays available.
info.triggered: Action-triggered jobs only start when you (or another workspace user) do something — import a file, activate an AI profile, launch an export. They have no system switch here: you enable or disable them where you already configure them (the workspace AI profile, the Google integration). Here you only see their operational parameters.
info.lock: The padlock on a parameter (including the frequency of scheduled jobs) means the value can't be changed from here: it's fixed in the worker's code and changing it takes more than a simple save.
